check.reason: The target is hospitals and their lobbying, and patients are treated as the ones the system fails. It has no invented numbers or quotes, doesn't mock the reporter, and avoids death, children and violence. The 'relief from relief' wordplay and the closing line about who gets screened for relief are dry and deadpan, so it counts as satire. The claim that hospitals want the law rolled back over federal cuts is a factual assertion we can't verify from the headline alone, so it's worth a quick check against the article before recording.

pick.title: States Are Forcing Hospitals To Offer More People Financial Aid. In Oregon, It’s Working.
pick.headline: Oregon Financial Aid Law Works; Hospitals Seek Relief From Relief
pick.take: Oregon required hospitals to screen patients for aid they might already qualify for, and patients got immediate relief. Hospitals now want the law rolled back, citing federal cuts. Relief is clearly available in this system. The only open question is who gets screened for it.
